Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Wong, Head of Distribution; Robert Kline, Head of Operations; and Elena Vasquez, Head of Risk Management.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by strong market appreciation and robust net inflows across our diversified product suite. Our AUM grew to $1.45 trillion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $1.1 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM, stabilizing fee rates in our high-margin alternatives segment, and positive operating leverage from tech efficiencies. Our expenses were $750 million, resulting in net income of $280 million. Our expense ratio improved due to scaled automation in back-office functions and disciplined cost management amid fee pressures.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for that overview. As your CFO, I'll dive deeper into the key drivers behind our assets under management, or AUM, focusing on the impact of market performance and net flows. Ending AUM reached $1.45 trillion as of September 30, 2024, up 4% quarter-over-quarter and 16% year-over-year. This reflects a powerful mix of positive net flows and supportive market returns in a volatile environment.

Our AUM reconciliation shows net flows of $32 billion in the quarter and $85 billion year-to-date, our strongest in recent years, outpacing industry averages. Equities led with $18 billion in flows, particularly our S&P 500 ETF which captured significant creations amid the Magnificent Seven rally. Fixed income rebounded with $5 billion, while alternatives and multi-asset shone with $9 billion, tapping into private credit and infrastructure opportunities.

Market performance added $38 billion in the quarter, dominated by a 3% lift from equities as the S&P 500 advanced on AI momentum. Fixed income turned positive late-quarter on rate cut signals, and alternatives buffered via mark-ups. FX shaved a bit off due to euro and yen weakness, but hedged classes mitigated much of it.

Turning to AUM growth and geographic breakdown, North America at 60% or $870 billion grew 18% year-over-year, driven by ETF inflows and institutional mandates. Europe at 25% or $362 billion rose 12%, boosted by UCITS ESG products. Asia-Pacific at 10% or $145 billion surged 22%, with sovereign wins and China access. Rest of world added steady growth via private markets.

On fund performance relative to peers and benchmarks, our Core Equity Fund returned 18.2% YTD, beating the Russell 1000 by 320 bps and peers by wider margins, thanks to quality growth picks like NVIDIA. SMID strategies excelled at 22.4% versus 12.8% for the Russell 2000. Global equities outperformed MSCI ACWI ex-US by 210 bps. Fixed income held up with 6.8% in IG corporates, topping benchmarks by 90 bps. Alternatives delivered 9.5%, outpacing HFRI. Overall, 79% of equity AUM rates 4- or 5-stars per Morningstar.

Our capital allocation strategy prioritizes shareholder returns with $2.8 billion returned year-to-date via buybacks at a discount and a 3.2% dividend yield. Organic investments of $450 million target digital platforms and regional expansion, like ETFs in Americas and ESG in EMEA. Strategic M&A added $1.2 billion in tuck-ins for alternatives scale. Balance sheet remains fortress-like with $3.5 billion cash.

Technology investments totaled $285 million this year, migrating to cloud for real-time NAVs, enhancing client portals for tax optimization, and deploying AI for alpha in quants. Robo-advisory now at $85 billion, with blockchain pilots cutting settlement times.

Net flows by channel: institutional $10.1 billion, led by LDI and fixed income; retail $4.4 billion via ETFs and SMAs; alternatives $0.7 billion in privates despite hedge outflows. This diversification fuels our momentum.

David Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by overweighting quality growth amid AI tailwinds while hedging volatility through options and derisking EM to 8%. We launched a tokenized real-world asset fund this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $500 million in commitments already, tapping into blockchain custody for yields with liquidity.

Lisa Wong: Thank you, David. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in Asia-Pacific are paying off, as evidenced by $12 billion in net new money from sovereign wealth funds and onshore China access, alongside UCITS growth in Europe where ESG mandates added €20 billion potential.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure, fully migrating to hybrid cloud and Snowflake for data, slashing processing times and enabling T+1 readiness. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on AI-powered robo-advisory and zero-touch onboarding, cutting acquisition costs by 30% and lifting retention to 98%.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Robert. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of geopolitical and interest rate risks and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes proprietary climate scoring in 70% of allocations, VaR limits below peers, and currency hedges now at 40% of international books.

Sarah Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. Thank you, everyone on the team, for that thorough review of our Q3 results. Before we open the line for questions, I'd like to outline our key priorities and strategic initiatives for the next 12 to 18 months. We closed the quarter with $1.45 trillion in AUM, up 16% year-over-year, fueled by $85 billion in net inflows and market gains during the S&P 500's strong rally. Yet we're pushing forward in a landscape of 2.5-3% inflation, expected Fed cuts to 4.25-4.50% by mid-2025, and rotations into value and small-caps, all while fees compress to 38 bps industry-wide.

Priority one: Accelerate organic AUM growth to $60-75 billion in inflows, targeting 10-12% expansion to $1.6-$1.7 trillion by end-2025. High-margin ETFs at 35% of AUM drove $12 billion YTD, and alternatives scale in private credit and infrastructure eyes the $1.5 trillion dry powder. Our Core Equity ETF beat Russell 1000 by 250 bps, challenging low-cost leaders.

Regionally, North America at 65% of inflows shifts to EMEA and APAC: €20 billion in Europe via Paris hub and UCITS actives for the €15 trillion market; $15 billion in APAC through JVs like semiconductors and renewables amid China's stimulus boosting retail equities 25%.

Priority two: Product innovation with five Q1 2025 launches—a $5 billion private credit fund at 9-11% IRR rivaling Ares; ESG multi-asset ETF 50% lower carbon; tokenized RWA on blockchain with Securitize for 7-9% yields in the $10 trillion market. Builds on ML alpha adding 120 bps via alt data like satellites.

Priority three: $250 million over two years in Apex Digital Horizon for AI robo-advisory at 95% volatility accuracy, targeting $100 billion RIA growth; cloud risk analytics for stress tests; API onboarding saving $150 million annually, holding margins at 35-37%.

Priority four: Derisk EM to 8%, overweight U.S. duration at 6.5 years, ESG AUM to $120 billion with climate scoring. Recruit 200 quants from top firms for Sharpe edge.

Financially, guide 8-10% fee growth, EPS $4.80-$5.20, ROE >18%, $2.80 dividend, $500 million buyback. This outpaces peers like T. Rowe and Invesco.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the impact of market performance and net flows on AUM?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, John. Michael, why don't you take that?

Michael Chen: Happy to. As I detailed earlier, our $1.45 trillion ending AUM blended $32 billion Q3 net flows—highest since post-pandemic—with $38 billion market gains. Equities contributed two-thirds of performance lift on the S&P rally, fixed income recovered on Fed signals, and alts buffered. Flows skewed to retail ETFs at 45%, institutional 35%, wealth 20%. Year-to-date $85 billion outran Morningstar's 8-10% industry pace, validating innovation like five new ETFs and robo-integration driving $10 billion micro-flows. FX hedgies contained drags. Forward, $90-110 billion expected in 2025 with BTC ETF tailwinds.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up—what's the geographic breakdown in that growth?

Michael Chen: North America 60% at $870 billion up 18% on tech ETFs; Europe 25% $362 billion +12% via ESG UCITS; APAC 10% $145 billion fastest at 22% from SWFs and China stimulus; rest 5% steady in privates. Global Alpha 3.0—innovation, tech, distribution—targets 12-15% FY2025 growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morningstar.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Core Equity Fund?

David Patel: Good morning, Emily. Our Core Equity returned 18.2% YTD net, +320 bps over Russell 1000 and +360 bps vs. peer median. NVIDIA/ASML overweight added 450 bps on AI; three-year Sharpe 1.25 tops 0.98 peers. SMID at 22.4% crushed Russell 2000 by 960 bps via industrials rotation. Global beat MSCI ex-US by 210 bps, Europe STOXX by 300 bps on renewables. FI IG corporates +90 bps Bloomberg, HY +110 bps. Alts 9.5% tops HFRI 250 bps. 79% 4/5-star equity AUM, quant ML boosts info ratio to 0.65, ESG adds 180 bps. Positioned for 2025 with tech overweight, FI neutral, alts to 20%.

Emily Chen: And how is the new tokenized RWA product performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Wong: Exceeding, Emily. $500 million committed early, on track for $3 billion year-one versus plan, as HNW seek 7-9% yields with daily liquidity via Securitize custody. Complements privates push, mirroring BlackRock BUIDL, with strong APAC/EMEA uptake amid $10 trillion RWA projection.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Robert Kline: Sure, David. Tech migration to AWS/Snowflake cut ETL to 2 hours, enabling real-time NAV for $450 billion ETFs and T+1 prep. Client portal at 72% SMA adoption harvested $1.2 billion tax losses, +120 bps after-tax. AI robo at $85 billion up 40%, mobile downloads +45%. Middle/back-office costs down 22%, flows up 17% from digital. $285 million capex yields 3.2x ROI, ramping to $320 million for tokenization targeting $50 billion digitized alts by 2026.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays.

Maria Gonzalez: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Maria. Robust framework enhanced for regs like MiFID II/SFDR—98% ESG coverage unlocked €15 billion flows. Geopolitics: EM cut to 8%, Middle East/energy hedges. Rates: duration 6.5 years FI, VaR 8.2% below peers. Cyber zero-trust post-breaches, SOC2 compliant. Climate scoring in 70% allocations, currency hedges 40%. Downside proven: -2.1% Q1 drawdown vs. S&P -4.5%. Aladdin integration cuts VaR errors 35%.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
